'''Vanina Ruhlmann-Kleider''' (born 1961){{r|born}} is a French physicist and director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), at [[CEA Paris-Saclay]]. Originally working in [[experimental particle physics]], her interests shifted to [[observational cosmology]] through her participation in the [[Supernova Legacy Survey]] and [[Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey]] projects.{{r|eph}}

==Education and career==
Ruhlmann-Kleider earned a [[diplôme d'études approfondies]] in nuclear and particle physics through her studies at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]], and in 1988 completed a doctorate through the [[University of Paris]],{{r|argent}} for research at CEA Paris-Saclay, with the dissertation ''Measurement of the strong running coupling constant from W and Z production (UA2 experiment)'' directed by André Roussarie.{{r|diss}} In the same year, she became a permanent researcher at CEA Paris-Saclay.{{r|argent}}

Until 2008, her research included experimental high-energy physics at [[CERN]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vanina Ruhlmann-Kleider INSPIRE author profile |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/990963 |access-date=2024-02-26 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> including the search for the [[Higgs Boson]]. She began work on the [[Supernova Legacy Survey]] in 2006, and since then has continued her research in observational cosmology.{{r|eph}} More recently, her work on the [[Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey]] has led to new insights into [[dark energy]].{{r|dark}} She is one of the group leaders of the SPP Cosmology group in the CEA Institute of research into the fundamental laws of the universe (IRFU).{{r|cosmo}}

==Recognition==
Ruhlmann-Kleider received the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques]] in 2002, and the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2003.{{r|argent}} She was named a chevalier in the [[Legion of Honour]] in 2010.{{r|lh}}
